concept.name: Higher low
concept.definition: A swing low that forms above the previous swing low. Together with higher highs, a sequence of higher lows constitutes the structural definition of an uptrend and shows declining selling pressure on pullbacks.
concept.intuition: Each dip finds buyers sooner than the last — the floor keeps rising.
concept.mechanics: Identified by comparing successive reaction troughs: when the latest pullback low holds above the prior low, a higher low is printed. A break below the most recent higher low is conventionally treated as a warning that the uptrend structure may be changing.
concept.failure_modes: Higher lows fail routinely as support on retest; a marginal undercut of the prior low can be stop-driven noise rather than a genuine structure break.
concept.misconceptions: That a higher low is a safe, low-risk entry point by itself; it is a structural observation, not a signal with defined risk.
concept.example: A stock pulls back to 54 after previously bottoming at 52, then rallies: the higher low at 54 preserves the uptrend structure.
